concepts.name: Reading a data table
concepts.definition_en: Reading a data table means locating the exact value at the intersection of the correct row and column, and using the table title, headings and units to interpret what that value measures.
concepts.explanation_hi: Table mein sahi row aur sahi column ka crossing point dhoondho, heading aur unit bhi padho, tabhi value ka matlab samajh aayega.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Reading a bar graph
concepts.definition_en: Reading a bar graph means comparing bar lengths or heights against the scale on the axis to read each category's value, and noting whether bars are vertical or horizontal and whether the scale starts at zero.
concepts.explanation_hi: Bar ki lambai ko axis ke scale se milao, kaunsi bar sabse badi ya chhoti hai ye scale dekh kar tay karo, andaza mat lagao.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Reading a line graph
concepts.definition_en: Reading a line graph means reading each plotted point against both axes and following the slope between points to see whether a quantity rises, falls or stays flat over time or categories.
concepts.explanation_hi: Line graph mein har point ko dono axis se padho aur slope dekho, upar ja rahi line badhotri aur neeche ja rahi line girawat dikhati hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Reading a pie chart
concepts.definition_en: Reading a pie chart means interpreting each sector by its share of the whole circle, where the full circle represents 100 percent or 360 degrees and each sector's size is proportional to its value.
concepts.explanation_hi: Pie chart mein poora circle 100 percent hota hai, jo sector jitna bada utna uska hissa bada, angle aur percent dono se value nikal sakti hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Percentage change within data
concepts.definition_en: Percentage change within data is the change in a charted or tabulated value from an earlier value to a later value, expressed as a percentage of the earlier value.
concepts.explanation_hi: Data mein badlav nikalne ke liye naya minus purana karo aur purane value se bhaag dekar 100 se guna karo, base hamesha purana value hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Ratio within data
concepts.definition_en: Ratio within data is the comparison of two values taken from a table or chart, written in simplest form, showing how many times one value is contained in the other.
concepts.explanation_hi: Data ke do values ka ratio nikalne ke liye dono ko unke common factor se kaat kar simplest form mein likho.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Average within data
concepts.definition_en: Average within data is the sum of a set of values read from a table or chart divided by the number of those values, giving a single representative value for the set.
concepts.explanation_hi: Chart ya table se saari values uthao, unka total karo aur kitni values hain usse bhaag do, yahi average hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Share of a category
concepts.definition_en: Share of a category is a single category's value expressed as a fraction or percentage of the total of all categories in the data set.
concepts.explanation_hi: Kisi ek category ka hissa nikalne ke liye uski value ko total se bhaag do, percent chahiye to 100 se guna karo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Missing-data inference
concepts.definition_en: Missing-data inference is recovering a blank or unstated value in a data set by using totals, averages, ratios or percentage relations that the given data must satisfy.
concepts.explanation_hi: Jahan value khaali hai wahan total, average ya ratio wale relation se peeche se hisaab lagao aur gayab number wapas nikalo.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE depth (banking advanced-DI module, retained from taxonomy v1.2)

concepts.name: Caselet arithmetic
concepts.definition_en: Caselet arithmetic is applying percentage, ratio and average calculations to numerical data given as a paragraph of text rather than as a table or chart, after first organising the paragraph's numbers into usable values.
concepts.explanation_hi: Caselet mein numbers paragraph mein chhupe hote hain, pehle unko alag-alag note karo phir un par percent, ratio ya average wala hisaab lagao.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE-except: MTS, GD (caselet arithmetic itself is general; its depth in SSC/Railway is basic); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Reading a radar chart
concepts.definition_en: Reading a radar chart means reading values plotted on several axes radiating from a common centre, where distance from the centre along each axis shows that variable's value and the joined shape allows comparison across variables.
concepts.explanation_hi: Radar chart mein centre se jitni door point hai utni us variable ki value badi hai, har axis ko alag padho phir shape se compare karo.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE depth (banking advanced-DI module, retained from taxonomy v1.2)

concepts.name: Arithmetic DI
concepts.definition_en: Arithmetic DI is data interpretation in which charted or tabulated values are not final answers but inputs to multi-step arithmetic, such as combining percentage change, ratio and average operations on the same data set.
concepts.explanation_hi: Arithmetic DI mein chart se value uthana sirf shuruaat hai, uske baad us par do-teen hisaab ek saath lagane padte hain tabhi jawab milta hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE depth (banking advanced-DI module, retained from taxonomy v1.2)

concepts.name: Data sufficiency judgement
concepts.definition_en: Data sufficiency judgement is deciding whether the statements and data given are enough, alone or together, to answer a question uniquely, without actually computing the final answer when sufficiency is all that is asked.
concepts.explanation_hi: Data sufficiency mein jawab nikalna nahi hai, sirf ye tay karna hai ki diye gaye statements se sawal ka ek pakka jawab mil sakta hai ya nahi.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE depth (banking advanced-DI module, retained from taxonomy v1.2)

concepts.name: Mean of raw data
concepts.definition_en: The mean of raw data is the sum of all observations divided by the number of observations, giving the arithmetic average of the data set.
concepts.explanation_hi: Raw data ka mean nikalne ke liye saare numbers jodo aur kitne numbers hain usse bhaag do.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Mean of grouped data
concepts.definition_en: The mean of grouped data is the sum of each class mark multiplied by its frequency, divided by the total frequency, where the class mark is the midpoint of the class interval.
concepts.explanation_hi: Grouped data mein har class ka midpoint nikalo, usko uski frequency se guna karo, sab jodo aur total frequency se bhaag do.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Median of raw data
concepts.definition_en: The median of raw data is the middle observation when the observations are arranged in ascending or descending order, or the average of the two middle observations when the count is even.
concepts.explanation_hi: Median ke liye numbers ko chhote se bade kram mein lagao, beech wala number median hai, aur agar count even hai to beech ke do numbers ka average lo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Median of grouped data
concepts.definition_en: The median of grouped data is found from the median class, the class containing the cumulative frequency that first reaches half the total frequency, using its lower limit, cumulative frequency before it, its frequency and its class width.
concepts.explanation_hi: Grouped median mein pehle median class dhoondho jahan cumulative frequency total ke aadhe tak pahunche, phir formula se median nikalo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Mode of raw data
concepts.definition_en: The mode of raw data is the observation that occurs most frequently in the data set; a data set may have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode.
concepts.explanation_hi: Mode woh number hai jo data mein sabse zyada baar aata hai, sabse zyada repeat hone wala hi mode hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Mode of grouped data
concepts.definition_en: The mode of grouped data is found from the modal class, the class with the highest frequency, using its lower limit, its frequency, the frequencies of the neighbouring classes and the class width.
concepts.explanation_hi: Grouped mode mein sabse zyada frequency wali class modal class hoti hai, phir uske aas-paas ki frequency se formula lagakar mode nikalo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Frequency tables
concepts.definition_en: A frequency table organises raw data into values or class intervals with the count of observations in each, and cumulative frequency adds each frequency to all frequencies before it.
concepts.explanation_hi: Frequency table mein har value ya class ke saamne likho ki woh kitni baar aayi hai, cumulative frequency mein peeche ki saari frequency jodte jao.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Basic data representation
concepts.definition_en: Basic data representation is presenting a frequency distribution or data set in an organised visual or tabular form, such as a table, bar diagram or pictorial summary, so that its pattern can be read at a glance.
concepts.explanation_hi: Data representation ka matlab hai numbers ko table ya diagram mein aise sajana ki ek nazar mein pattern samajh aa jaye.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Range
concepts.definition_en: The range of a data set is the difference between its largest observation and its smallest observation, giving the simplest measure of how spread out the data are.
concepts.explanation_hi: Range nikalne ke liye sabse bade number mein se sabse chhota number ghata do, yahi data ka failaav batata hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: nth term of an AP
concepts.definition_en: The nth term of an arithmetic progression is the term in position n, found from the first term and the common difference added repeatedly, with each step adding the same amount.
concepts.explanation_hi: AP ka n-th term nikalne ke liye pehle term mein common difference ko (n-1) baar jodo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Sum of an AP
concepts.definition_en: The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression is the average of the first and last terms multiplied by the number of terms, equivalently expressed using the first term and common difference.
concepts.explanation_hi: AP ke pehle n terms ka sum nikalne ke liye pehle aur aakhri term ka average lo aur n se guna karo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Common difference of an AP
concepts.definition_en: The common difference of an arithmetic progression is the fixed amount added to each term to get the next term, found by subtracting any term from the term that follows it.
concepts.explanation_hi: AP mein common difference nikalne ke liye kisi bhi term ko usse pehle wale term se ghata do, har jagah ek hi antar milega.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: nth term of a GP
concepts.definition_en: The nth term of a geometric progression is the term in position n, found from the first term multiplied repeatedly by the common ratio, with each step multiplying by the same amount.
concepts.explanation_hi: GP ka n-th term nikalne ke liye pehle term ko common ratio ki power (n-1) se guna karo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Sum of a GP
concepts.definition_en: The sum of the first n terms of a geometric progression is found by a formula using the first term, the common ratio and the number of terms, with a separate form when the common ratio equals 1.
concepts.explanation_hi: GP ke pehle n terms ka sum nikalne ke liye pehla term, common ratio aur n wala formula lagao, aur agar ratio 1 hai to sum seedha n guna pehla term hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Common ratio of a GP
concepts.definition_en: The common ratio of a geometric progression is the fixed amount by which each term is multiplied to get the next term, found by dividing any term by the term that precedes it.
concepts.explanation_hi: GP mein common ratio nikalne ke liye kisi bhi term ko usse pehle wale term se bhaag do, har jagah ek hi ratio milega.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Missing term in a series
concepts.definition_en: A missing term in a series is the term that completes the series pattern, found by identifying the rule governing the given terms, such as a common difference or common ratio, and applying it at the gap.
concepts.explanation_hi: Series mein khaali jagah bharne ke liye pehle pattern pehchano, antar ya ratio ek jaisa hai ya nahi dekho, phir wahi rule gap par lagao.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Wrong term in a series
concepts.definition_en: A wrong term in a series is the single term that breaks the series pattern, found by generating the expected terms from the identified rule and comparing each given term against its expected value.
concepts.explanation_hi: Wrong term dhoondhne ke liye poori series ka pattern nikal kar har term ko check karo, jo term pattern se alag hai wahi galat term hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE (NTPC scope; verify against corpus in Phase 3; MTS/GD coverage TBD); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Sample space and favourable outcomes
concepts.definition_en: The sample space of an experiment is the set of all possible outcomes, and the favourable outcomes are those outcomes in the sample space that satisfy the event being considered.
concepts.explanation_hi: Sample space ka matlab hai experiment ke saare possible natije, aur favourable outcomes woh natije hain jo hamare event se match karte hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Probability of an event
concepts.definition_en: The probability of an event is the number of favourable outcomes for that event divided by the total number of possible outcomes in the sample space, assuming all outcomes are equally likely.
concepts.explanation_hi: Probability nikalne ke liye favourable outcomes ko total possible outcomes se bhaag do, bas dhyan rakho saare natije equally likely hone chahiye.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Complementary events
concepts.definition_en: The complement of an event is the event that the original event does not occur, and its probability is one minus the probability of the original event.
concepts.explanation_hi: Agar event ke hone ki probability pata hai to na hone ki probability 1 mein se woh ghata kar mil jati hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Dice problems
concepts.definition_en: Dice problems apply probability to the outcomes of throwing one or more fair dice, where each die has six equally likely faces numbered 1 to 6 and the sample space is built from all face combinations.
concepts.explanation_hi: Dice wale sawal mein har die ke 6 faces equally likely hote hain, total outcomes ke hisaab se favourable faces gin kar probability nikalo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Coin problems
concepts.definition_en: Coin problems apply probability to the outcomes of tossing one or more fair coins, where each toss has two equally likely outcomes, head or tail, and repeated tosses multiply the total outcomes.
concepts.explanation_hi: Coin wale sawal mein har toss mein head ya tail aane ke barabar chance hote hain, total outcomes gin kar favourable se bhaag do.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Card problems
concepts.definition_en: Card problems apply probability to drawing cards from a standard pack of 52 cards, organised into four suits of 13 cards each, with face cards, numbered cards and colour groups counted from that structure.
concepts.explanation_hi: Card wale sawal mein poori pack 52 cards ki hoti hai, chaar suits aur har suit mein 13 cards hote hain, isi structure se favourable cards gino.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Balls from a bag or urn
concepts.definition_en: Balls-from-a-bag problems apply probability to drawing balls of given colours from a bag or urn, where favourable outcomes are the balls of the required colour and total outcomes are all balls in the bag.
concepts.explanation_hi: Bag wale sawal mein chahiye wale colour ki balls favourable hoti hain aur bag ki total balls denominator hoti hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Odds in favour and against
concepts.definition_en: Odds in favour of an event are the ratio of favourable outcomes to unfavourable outcomes, and odds against are the reverse ratio, both convertible to probability and back.
concepts.explanation_hi: Odds ka matlab hai favourable aur unfavourable outcomes ka ratio, favour mein ulte se alag hota hai aur isko probability mein bhi badla ja sakta hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Independent events
concepts.definition_en: Independent events are events where the outcome of one event does not affect the probability of the other event, so their joint probability is the product of their separate probabilities.
concepts.explanation_hi: Independent events mein ek event ka natija doosre ki probability ko badalta nahi hai, isliye dono ki probability ko guna kar do.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Dependent events
concepts.definition_en: Dependent events are events where the outcome of one event changes the probability of the other event, so the second event's probability must be evaluated under the changed conditions.
concepts.explanation_hi: Dependent events mein pehle event ka natija doosre event ki probability badal deta hai, isliye doosri probability nayi situation ke hisaab se nikalo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Multiplication rule (AND)
concepts.definition_en: The multiplication rule gives the probability that two events both occur, as the probability of the first event multiplied by the probability of the second event given the first, simplifying to a plain product for independent events.
concepts.explanation_hi: AND wala sawal ho to dono events ki probability ko guna karo, dependent case mein doosri probability pehle ke baad wali situation se lo.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Addition rule (OR)
concepts.definition_en: The addition rule gives the probability that at least one of two events occurs, as the sum of their probabilities minus the probability that both occur, with the subtraction dropped when the events are mutually exclusive.
concepts.explanation_hi: OR wala sawal ho to dono ki probability jodo aur dono ke ek saath hone wali probability ghata do, warna double counting ho jayegi.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Drawing with replacement
concepts.definition_en: Drawing with replacement means each drawn item is returned to the set before the next draw, so the total number of outcomes and the composition stay the same for every draw and successive draws are independent.
concepts.explanation_hi: With replacement mein nikali cheez wapas rakh di jati hai, isliye har draw mein total aur composition ek jaise rehte hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Drawing without replacement
concepts.definition_en: Drawing without replacement means each drawn item is kept out of the set, so the total number of outcomes and the composition change after every draw and successive draws are dependent.
concepts.explanation_hi: Without replacement mein nikali cheez wapas nahi rakhi jati, isliye har draw ke baad total kam ho jata hai aur doosri probability badal jati hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Conditional probability
concepts.definition_en: Conditional probability P(A|B) is the probability that event A occurs given that event B has already occurred, found by restricting the sample space to the outcomes where B occurs.
concepts.explanation_hi: Conditional probability mein ek event ke ho jaane ke baad doosre event ki probability nikalte hain, sample space sirf us pehli condition tak simat jata hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE-except: MTS, GD (advanced depth, TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Bayes' theorem (basic)
concepts.definition_en: Bayes' theorem reverses a conditional probability, giving the probability of a cause given an observed outcome from the prior probability of the cause, the likelihood of the outcome under that cause, and the overall probability of the outcome.
concepts.explanation_hi: Bayes theorem se ulta hisaab lagta hai, natija dekh kar ye pata chalta hai ki kaunsi wajah kitni sambhav thi.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE-except: MTS, GD (advanced depth, TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus); PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Counting outcomes with permutations and combinations
concepts.definition_en: Counting outcomes with permutations and combinations is finding the number of favourable and total outcomes by counting arrangements and selections, using permutations when order matters and combinations when order does not matter.
concepts.explanation_hi: Jab outcomes ginna mushkil ho to permutation-combination se gino, order matter kare to permutation aur na kare to combination lagao.
concepts.exam_mapping: CORE; PARTIAL: MI Translator, Paramedical (combined sections, maths share per-question TBD); PROVISIONAL: Delhi Police HC

concepts.name: Fundamental counting principle
concepts.definition_en: If one task can be done in m ways and a second task, following it, in n ways, then the two tasks together can be done in m x n ways; the rule extends by multiplication to any number of successive tasks.
concepts.explanation_hi: Ek kaam m tareeke se aur uske baad doosra kaam n tareeke se ho sakta hai, to dono milkar m x n tareeke se honge.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Factorial n!
concepts.definition_en: For a positive integer n, n! is the product of all positive integers from 1 to n, and by convention 0! = 1.
concepts.explanation_hi: n! matlab 1 se n tak sab numbers ka guna, jaise 4! = 1 x 2 x 3 x 4 = 24, aur 0! = 1 hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Permutation P(n,r)
concepts.definition_en: P(n,r) is the number of ways of arranging r distinct objects chosen from n distinct objects, where the order of arrangement matters.
concepts.explanation_hi: P(n,r) matlab n cheezon me se r cheezon ko order ke saath sajana, kyunki yahan kaun pehle hai ye matter karta hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Arrangements with repetition
concepts.definition_en: When each of r positions can be filled by any of n objects independently, with repetition allowed, the number of arrangements is n raised to the power r.
concepts.explanation_hi: Jab har jagah par koi bhi cheez dobara use ho sakti hai, to r jagahon ke liye kul tareeke n ki power r hote hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Combination C(n,r)
concepts.definition_en: C(n,r) is the number of ways of selecting r objects from n distinct objects, where the order of selection does not matter.
concepts.explanation_hi: C(n,r) matlab n cheezon me se r cheezon ko chunna, jahan order se koi farq nahi padta, sirf kaun chuna gaya ye matter karta hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Complementary combinations C(n,r) = C(n,n-r)
concepts.definition_en: Choosing r objects from n is the same as leaving out the other n-r objects, so C(n,r) equals C(n,n-r).
concepts.explanation_hi: n me se r chunna aur n-r ko chhodna ek hi baat hai, isliye C(n,r) = C(n,n-r) hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Circular permutation
concepts.definition_en: The number of ways of arranging n distinct objects around a circle, where only relative positions matter, is (n-1)!; if clockwise and anticlockwise arrangements are treated as identical, it is (n-1)!/2.
concepts.explanation_hi: Gol table par n logon ko bithane ke tareeke (n-1)! hote hain, kyunki sirf relative position matter karti hai, aur ulta-seedha ek maan lo to (n-1)!/2.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Selection vs arrangement distinction
concepts.definition_en: A counting problem uses combinations when only the chosen group matters and permutations when the order or position of the chosen objects also matters; applying a restriction (such as including or excluding a particular object) is handled by fixing that part first and then counting the rest.
concepts.explanation_hi: Sirf group chunna hai to combination, order ya position bhi matter karti hai to permutation; koi shart ho to pehle us hisse ko fix karo, phir baaki gino.
concepts.exam_mapping: TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (no in-scope exam asserts it in Phase 1 records; do not assume Technician Gr I)

concepts.name: Roster and set-builder notation
concepts.definition_en: A set can be written in roster form by listing its elements inside braces, or in set-builder form by stating the property that exactly its elements satisfy.
concepts.explanation_hi: Set ko do tareeke se likhte hain: roster me saare elements list karke, set-builder me wo property likhkar jo sirf uske elements me ho.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Subsets
concepts.definition_en: Set A is a subset of set B if every element of A is also an element of B; the empty set is a subset of every set, and a set with n elements has 2^n subsets.
concepts.explanation_hi: A, B ka subset hai agar A ka har element B me bhi ho; khaali set har set ka subset hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Union, intersection and complement
concepts.definition_en: The union A union B contains elements in A or B or both; the intersection A intersect B contains elements in both A and B; the complement of A contains all elements of the universal set that are not in A.
concepts.explanation_hi: Union matlab A ya B me se kisi me ho, intersection matlab dono me ho, complement matlab universal set me ho par A me na ho.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Inclusion-exclusion for two sets
concepts.definition_en: The number of elements in the union of two finite sets equals the sum of their sizes minus the size of their intersection, because elements in both sets would otherwise be counted twice.
concepts.explanation_hi: Do sets ke union ke elements = dono ke elements ka jod minus common elements, kyunki common wale do baar gin jaate hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Venn diagram reasoning
concepts.definition_en: A Venn diagram represents sets as overlapping regions, so counts for exactly one set, exactly both sets, or neither can be read off by filling the overlapping region first and then working outwards.
concepts.explanation_hi: Venn diagram me sets ko overlapping golon se dikhate hain; pehle common hissa bharo, phir baahar ki taraf counts nikalo.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Relations (basic)
concepts.definition_en: A relation from set A to set B is a subset of the Cartesian product A x B, that is, a collection of ordered pairs (a, b) with a in A and b in B.
concepts.explanation_hi: Relation matlab A se B tak ke ordered pairs ka ek group, jahan pehla element A se aur doosra B se ho.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Functions (basic)
concepts.definition_en: A function from set A to set B is a relation in which every element of A is paired with exactly one element of B.
concepts.explanation_hi: Function ek aisa relation hai jisme A ke har element ki jodi B ke sirf ek hi element se hoti hai, na zero se na do se.
concepts.exam_mapping: NAMED: Technician Grade I (extension, per master list C5) + TBD — needs Phase 3 corpus (other in-scope exams unverified)

concepts.name: Matrix types
concepts.definition_en: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers; common types are row, column, square, zero, diagonal, scalar and identity matrices, classified by their order and by which entries are zero or equal.
concepts.explanation_hi: Matrix numbers ki ek aayatakar table hoti hai; row, column, square, zero, diagonal aur identity uske khaas types hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Matrix addition
concepts.definition_en: Two matrices of the same order are added by adding their corresponding entries, and the result has the same order as the original matrices.
concepts.explanation_hi: Do matrices ko tabhi jod sakte hain jab dono ka order same ho, aur jod har corresponding entry ko jodkar hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Matrix multiplication
concepts.definition_en: The product AB is defined only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B, and its (i,j) entry is the sum of products of row i of A with column j of B; matrix multiplication is generally not commutative.
concepts.explanation_hi: AB tabhi banta hai jab A ke columns B ke rows ke barabar hon; har entry row aur column ke guna ka jod hoti hai, aur AB hamesha BA ke barabar nahi hota.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Transpose of a matrix
concepts.definition_en: The transpose of a matrix is obtained by interchanging its rows and columns, so the (i,j) entry of A becomes the (j,i) entry of A transpose.
concepts.explanation_hi: Transpose matlab matrix ki rows ko columns bana dena, pehli row pehla column ban jaati hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Determinant of a 2x2 matrix
concepts.definition_en: The determinant of a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] is ad - bc, and it is zero exactly when the rows (or columns) are proportional.
concepts.explanation_hi: 2x2 matrix ka determinant ad minus bc hota hai; ye zero tab hota hai jab rows ek doosre ki multiple hon.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Determinant of a 3x3 matrix
concepts.definition_en: The determinant of a 3x3 matrix is found by expanding along any row or column: each entry multiplied by its cofactor (with alternating signs) and summed.
concepts.explanation_hi: 3x3 ka determinant kisi bhi row ya column se nikalte hain: har entry ko uske cofactor se guna karke, plus-minus sign ke saath, sab jod do.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Properties of determinants
concepts.definition_en: Interchanging two rows or columns changes the sign of a determinant; a determinant with two identical rows or columns is zero; multiplying a row by a scalar multiplies the determinant by that scalar; and det(AB) = det(A) x det(B).
concepts.explanation_hi: Do rows badlo to sign badalta hai, do rows same hon to determinant zero, ek row ko k se guna karo to determinant bhi k guna ho jaata hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Adjoint and inverse of a matrix
concepts.definition_en: The adjoint of a square matrix is the transpose of its cofactor matrix, and the inverse exists exactly when the determinant is non-zero, given by A inverse = adjoint(A) / det(A).
concepts.explanation_hi: Adjoint matlab cofactor matrix ka transpose, aur inverse tabhi milta hai jab determinant zero na ho: inverse = adjoint / determinant.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Solving linear systems via matrices and Cramer rule
concepts.definition_en: A system of linear equations written as AX = B has the solution X = A inverse B when A is invertible; Cramer's rule gives each unknown as a ratio of determinants, with the determinant of A in the denominator.
concepts.explanation_hi: Equations ko AX = B likho, phir X = A inverse B se jawab milta hai; Cramer rule me har unknown ek determinant ka ratio hota hai, neeche A ka determinant.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Imaginary unit i
concepts.definition_en: The imaginary unit i is defined by i squared = -1, so it provides square roots for negative numbers, which have no real square root.
concepts.explanation_hi: i ek aisi kalpana sankhya hai jiska square -1 hota hai, isliye negative numbers ka bhi square root mil jaata hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Standard form a + ib
concepts.definition_en: Every complex number can be written uniquely as a + ib, where a is the real part, b is the imaginary part, and a and b are real numbers.
concepts.explanation_hi: Har complex number a + ib ke roop me likha jaata hai, jahan a real hissa aur b imaginary hisse ka coefficient hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Conjugate of a complex number
concepts.definition_en: The conjugate of a + ib is a - ib, obtained by changing the sign of the imaginary part; a number multiplied by its conjugate gives the sum of the squares of its parts.
concepts.explanation_hi: a + ib ka conjugate a - ib hota hai, bas imaginary hisse ka sign badal do; dono ka guna a square plus b square deta hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Multiplication of complex numbers
concepts.definition_en: Complex numbers are multiplied by expanding brackets as with binomials and replacing i squared by -1, collecting the real and imaginary parts separately.
concepts.explanation_hi: Complex numbers ko guna karte waqt brackets kholo jaise binomials me, phir i square ki jagah -1 rakhkar real aur imaginary hisse alag karo.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Division of complex numbers
concepts.definition_en: A complex number is divided by another by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, which turns the denominator into a real number.
concepts.explanation_hi: Complex number se bhaag dene ke liye upar-neeche denominator ke conjugate se guna karo, taaki neeche sirf real number reh jaaye.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Modulus of a complex number
concepts.definition_en: The modulus |z| of a + ib is its distance from the origin in the complex plane, equal to the square root of a squared plus b squared.
concepts.explanation_hi: Modulus matlab complex plane me origin se us point ki doori, jo root(a square plus b square) hoti hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Argument of a complex number
concepts.definition_en: The argument of a non-zero complex number is the angle its position vector makes with the positive real axis, usually taken in the interval (-pi, pi], and found from tan(theta) = b/a with the quadrant of (a, b) taken into account.
concepts.explanation_hi: Argument matlab wo angle jo complex number ka point positive real axis se banata hai; tan theta = b/a se milta hai, par quadrant dekhkar sahi angle chuno.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Powers of i
concepts.definition_en: Powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1, so any power i^n is found from the remainder of n on division by 4.
concepts.explanation_hi: i ki powers chaar ke cycle me ghoomti hain: i, -1, -i, 1; koi bhi i^n nikalne ke liye n ko 4 se bhaag dekar remainder dekho.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Square roots of complex numbers (basic)
concepts.definition_en: To find a square root of a complex number, assume the root is x + iy, square it, and equate real and imaginary parts to solve for x and y; a non-zero complex number has two opposite square roots.
concepts.explanation_hi: Complex number ka square root nikalne ke liye root ko x + iy maan lo, square karke real aur imaginary hisse barabar karo; har non-zero number ke do ulte square roots hote hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Vector notation and components
concepts.definition_en: A vector is a quantity with magnitude and direction, written in component form as xi + yj + zk or as a position vector from the origin to a point.
concepts.explanation_hi: Vector ek aisi quantity hai jisme magnitude aur direction dono hon; use xi + yj + zk ke roop me ya origin se point tak ke position vector se likhte hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Magnitude of a vector
concepts.definition_en: The magnitude (modulus) of a vector is its length, found from its components by the square root of the sum of their squares.
concepts.explanation_hi: Vector ki magnitude matlab uski lambai, jo components ke squares ke jod ka square root hoti hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Unit vector
concepts.definition_en: A unit vector has magnitude 1, and the unit vector in the direction of a non-zero vector a is a divided by its magnitude.
concepts.explanation_hi: Unit vector ki lambai 1 hoti hai; kisi vector ki direction ka unit vector us vector ko uski magnitude se bhaag dekar milta hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Vector addition and subtraction
concepts.definition_en: Vectors are added and subtracted component-wise, which matches the triangle and parallelogram laws geometrically; the vector from point A to point B is the position vector of B minus that of A.
concepts.explanation_hi: Vectors ko component-wise jodte-ghatate hain, jo triangle aur parallelogram law se bhi milta hai; A se B tak ka vector B ka position vector minus A ka position vector hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Collinearity of vectors and points
concepts.definition_en: Two vectors are collinear if one is a scalar multiple of the other, and three points are collinear if the vectors joining them are parallel.
concepts.explanation_hi: Do vectors collinear hain agar ek doosre ka scalar multiple ho; teen points collinear hain agar unko jodne wale vectors parallel hon.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Dot product (scalar product)
concepts.definition_en: The dot product of two vectors is a scalar equal to the product of their magnitudes and the cosine of the angle between them, and also equal to the sum of the products of corresponding components; it is zero exactly when the vectors are perpendicular.
concepts.explanation_hi: Dot product ek number hota hai: magnitudes ka guna into angle ka cosine, ya corresponding components ke guna ka jod; perpendicular vectors ka dot product zero hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Cross product (vector product)
concepts.definition_en: The cross product of two vectors is a vector of magnitude |a||b|sin(theta) in the direction perpendicular to both, given by the determinant of the unit vectors and components; it is zero exactly when the vectors are parallel.
concepts.explanation_hi: Cross product ek vector hota hai jo dono vectors par perpendicular hai, uski lambai |a||b|sin theta hoti hai aur use determinant se nikalte hain; parallel vectors ka cross product zero hota hai.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Coplanarity of vectors
concepts.definition_en: Three vectors are coplanar if their scalar triple product is zero, meaning one of them lies in the plane of the other two.
concepts.explanation_hi: Teen vectors coplanar hain agar unka scalar triple product zero ho, matlab teesra vector pehle do ke plane me hi ho.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Equations of lines in 3D
concepts.definition_en: A line in 3D through a point with position vector a and parallel to vector b has vector equation r = a + lambda b, and Cartesian form (x - x1)/l = (y - y1)/m = (z - z1)/n, where (l, m, n) are direction ratios.
concepts.explanation_hi: 3D me line ka equation r = a + lambda b hota hai, jahan a point ka position vector aur b direction vector hai; Cartesian roop me (x-x1)/l = (y-y1)/m = (z-z1)/n.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Equations of planes in 3D
concepts.definition_en: A plane through a point and perpendicular to a normal vector n has vector equation r . n = d and Cartesian equation ax + by + cz = d, where (a, b, c) are the direction ratios of the normal.
concepts.explanation_hi: Plane ka equation r . n = d hota hai, jahan n normal vector hai; Cartesian roop ax + by + cz = d hai, jahan (a,b,c) normal ke direction ratios hain.
concepts.exam_mapping: OUT-OF-SCOPE (NDA syllabus, retained from taxonomy v1.2; no in-scope exam)

concepts.name: Distance in 3D (basic)
concepts.definition_en: The distance between two points in 3D is the magnitude of their difference vector, and the distance from a point to a plane ax + by + cz = d is the absolute value of the plane expression at the point divided by the magnitude of the normal.
concepts.explanation_hi: 3D me do points ki doori unke difference vector ki lambai hoti hai, aur point se plane ki doori plane ke expression ka absolute value divided by normal ki lambai hoti hai.

concepts.name: Sphere in 3D (basic)
concepts.definition_en: A sphere with centre (a, b, c) and radius r is the set of points at distance r from the centre, with equation (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 + (z - c)^2 = r^2.
concepts.explanation_hi: Sphere un points ka set hai jo centre se r doori par hon; centre (a,b,c) aur radius r ho to equation (x-a)^2 + (y-b)^2 + (z-c)^2 = r^2 hoti hai.

concepts.name: Limit of a function
concepts.definition_en: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is the value f(x) gets arbitrarily close to as x gets arbitrarily close to a, whether or not f(a) itself is defined or equal to that value.
concepts.explanation_hi: Limit matlab jab x, a ke bahut kareeb jaaye to f(x) kis value ke kareeb jaata hai, chahe f(a) defined ho ya na ho.

concepts.name: Continuity of a function
concepts.definition_en: A function f is continuous at a point a if its limit as x approaches a exists and equals f(a), so the graph has no break or jump at that point.
concepts.explanation_hi: Function a par continuous hai agar uska limit f(a) ke barabar ho, matlab graph me us point par koi toot ya jump na ho.

concepts.name: Derivative as rate of change
concepts.definition_en: The derivative f'(x) is the instantaneous rate of change of f at x, defined as the limit of the difference quotient, and it gives the slope of the tangent to the graph of f at that point.
concepts.explanation_hi: Derivative matlab kisi point par function ke badalne ki instant speed, jo tangent ki slope bhi hoti hai.

concepts.name: Standard derivatives: polynomial and trigonometric
concepts.definition_en: The derivative of x^n is n x^(n-1); the derivative of sin x is cos x, of cos x is -sin x, and of tan x is sec^2 x.
concepts.explanation_hi: x^n ka derivative n x^(n-1) hota hai; sin ka cos, cos ka -sin, aur tan ka sec square hota hai.

concepts.name: Standard derivatives: exponential and logarithmic
concepts.definition_en: The derivative of e^x is e^x, of a^x is a^x ln a, and of ln x is 1/x for x > 0.
concepts.explanation_hi: e^x ka derivative wahi e^x hota hai, a^x ka a^x ln a, aur ln x ka 1/x hota hai.

concepts.name: Product and quotient rules
concepts.definition_en: The derivative of a product is the first function times the derivative of the second plus the second times the derivative of the first, and the derivative of a quotient follows the numerator-derivative minus denominator-derivative rule over the square of the denominator.
concepts.explanation_hi: Product ka derivative: pehla into doosre ka derivative plus doosra into pehle ka derivative; quotient me (neeche wala into upar ka derivative minus upar wala into neeche ka derivative) divided by neeche ka square.

concepts.name: Chain rule
concepts.definition_en: The derivative of a composite function f(g(x)) is f'(g(x)) multiplied by g'(x), that is, the outer derivative evaluated at the inner function times the derivative of the inner function.
concepts.explanation_hi: Chain rule matlab composite function ka derivative: baahar wale ka derivative (andar wala daalkar) into andar wale ka derivative.

concepts.name: Maxima and minima
concepts.definition_en: A differentiable function has local maxima or minima only at critical points where its derivative is zero (or undefined); the second derivative test says a critical point is a local maximum if f'' < 0 and a local minimum if f'' > 0.
concepts.explanation_hi: Maxima-minima wahi mil sakte hain jahan derivative zero ho; second derivative negative ho to maxima, positive ho to minima.

concepts.name: Standard integrals
concepts.definition_en: Integration reverses differentiation: the integral of x^n (n not -1) is x^(n+1)/(n+1), of 1/x is ln|x|, of sin x is -cos x, of cos x is sin x, and of e^x is e^x, each plus an arbitrary constant.
concepts.explanation_hi: Integration differentiation ka ulta hai: x^n ka integral x^(n+1)/(n+1), 1/x ka ln|x|, sin ka -cos, cos ka sin, e^x ka e^x, har ek ke saath + C.

concepts.name: Definite integrals
concepts.definition_en: The definite integral of f from a to b equals F(b) - F(a), where F is any antiderivative of f, and it gives the signed area between the curve and the x-axis over [a, b].
concepts.explanation_hi: Definite integral a se b tak F(b) minus F(a) hota hai, jahan F antiderivative hai; ye curve aur x-axis ke beech ka signed area deta hai.

concepts.name: Area under a curve
concepts.definition_en: The area between a non-negative curve y = f(x) and the x-axis from x = a to x = b is the definite integral of f over [a, b]; where the curve goes below the axis, the absolute value of the function is integrated so area stays positive.
concepts.explanation_hi: Curve aur x-axis ke beech ka area a se b tak f ka definite integral hota hai; jahan curve neeche ho wahan absolute value ka integral lo taaki area positive rahe.

concepts.name: Order and degree of a differential equation
concepts.definition_en: The order of a differential equation is the order of its highest derivative, and its degree is the power of that highest derivative once the equation is written free of radicals and fractions in the derivatives.
concepts.explanation_hi: Order matlab sabse bade derivative ka order, degree matlab us derivative ki power, jab equation me derivatives par koi root ya fraction na ho.

concepts.name: General and particular solutions (basic)
concepts.definition_en: The general solution of a differential equation contains as many arbitrary constants as the order of the equation, and a particular solution is obtained by fixing those constants from given conditions.
concepts.explanation_hi: General solution me order ke barabar arbitrary constants hote hain; di gayi conditions se un constants ki value fix karo to particular solution milta hai.
